name: blake2b-simd (Minio)
baseline: SHA-256 / SHA-512 (Go standard library crypto/sha256, crypto/sha512 — not OpenSSL)
workload: Hashing in-memory data with a pure-Go BLAKE2b implementation using hand-written AVX2/AVX/SSE assembly, compared to Go's standard-library SHA256/SHA512 and to the non-assembly Go BLAKE2b implementation.
claimed_speedup: BLAKE2b (AVX2): 850.64 MB/s vs SHA256 189.58 MB/s (4.5x) and SHA512 306.33 MB/s (2.8x); also 3.94x/3.28x/2.85x over pure-Go BLAKE2b for AVX2/AVX/SSE respectively
stars_or_usage: 255 stars; used internally by Minio for bitrot detection in its erasure-coded object storage
tradeoffs: Requires AVX2/AVX/SSE (auto-selects, falls back to generic); Go-assembly implementation increases maintenance burden; BLAKE2b is a different digest/algorithm than SHA-2, not a drop-in replacement where SHA-2 compliance (e.g. FIPS) is required.
caveats: No CPU model, compiler, or build flags stated in the post; the comparison baseline is Go's own crypto/sha256 and crypto/sha512, not OpenSSL, so it only partially matches the assignment's named baseline; original blog.minio.io domain is now dead (connection refused), content retrieved via Wayback Machine snapshot; repo archived with no commits since 2017.
found_via: Blogs/talks: HN Algolia query 'BLAKE2 fast' surfaced 'Fast hashing in Golang using BLAKE2' (blog.minio.io, 2016-07-06), full text retrieved via web.archive.org snapshot since the live blog is offline
